name: Dabrafenib + Trametinib (BRAF/MEK inhibitor, BRAF V600E/K melanoma)
cyclesNote: Continuous oral dosing: dabrafenib 150 mg twice daily plus trametinib 2 mg once daily (Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v2.2026, Table 19, MS-63 to MS-64). Adjuvant (resected stage III BRAF V600E/K): given for up to 1 year (COMBI-AD). Advanced (unresectable stage III / stage IV): continued until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity (COMBI-d, COMBI-v). The 28-day cycle is a scheduling container for continuous daily dosing.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: BRAF/MEK inhibitor combination REQUIRES a BRAF V600 activating mutation. This regimen is indicated for BRAF V600E or V600K mutation-positive disease: adjuvant (resected stage III, COMBI-AD) and unresectable/metastatic (COMBI-d, COMBI-v). Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Melanoma: Cutaneous, melanomas with BRAF V600E may derive higher adjuvant benefit than V600K (line 2629). Do NOT use in BRAF wild-type disease.

supportiveCare: Pyrexia management: dabrafenib/trametinib commonly cause recurrent fever; hold both drugs for fever and resume per labeling.

Baseline and periodic LVEF (echocardiogram) for trametinib-related cardiomyopathy; ophthalmologic assessment for retinal events; dermatologic surveillance for cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma/keratoacanthoma.
Monitor for MEK-inhibitor toxicities (rash, diarrhea, venous thromboembolism, retinal vein occlusion) per Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v2.2026, Table 21 (MS-66 onward).
monitoring: LFTs, CBC, glucose; clinical/radiographic response assessment

doseModificationRules.text: For fever, interrupt dabrafenib (and trametinib per labeling) and resume once resolved; prophylaxis/antipyretics per guidance.

doseModificationRules.condition: decline in LVEF or grade 3 to 4 non-cardiac toxicity
doseModificationRules.text: Hold or reduce trametinib for symptomatic or significant asymptomatic LVEF decline, or grade 3 to 4 toxicity, per labeling; obtain clinical review.

drugs.name: Dabrafenib
drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v2.2026, Table 19 (MS-63 to MS-64), treatment arm 'Dab (150 mg BID) + tram (2 mg QD)'. Dabrafenib 150 mg PO TWICE daily (BID) continuously; represented as days 1 to 28 of a 28-day cycle for scheduling. Taken orally; continuous dosing until progression or unacceptable toxicity (advanced) or for up to 1 year (adjuvant).
